_what: A macOS Seatbelt profile (/usr/bin/sandbox-exec) per native helper this Mac runs on content it did not make (computer/helper-sandbox.mjs). One row per helper: `allow` is the whole of what its profile permits on top of `deny default` (the entries were found by running the real helper under a deny-default profile and adding only what made it finish, then removing every entry that was not needed again), `{here}` is the folder the helper's program lives in. `confined` and `not_confined` say plainly what the profile does and does not hold, so the security claim is exact. `enabled` false runs the helper as before. The profile is built for each run; a helper with no row, or a Mac without sandbox-exec, is refused, never run unconfined.

image-text.what: Reads image bytes on standard input and answers the text found in them (computer/observe-visual.swift, run by /usr/bin/swift). It decodes pictures from anywhere, so a hostile picture reaches ImageIO and Vision.
confined: the network: no outbound or inbound connection
the person's files: nothing under their home folder can be read or written
files anywhere else on the disk: writes only to the per-user temporary folder
not_confined: mach services: any can be looked up (Vision and ImageIO need several; none was singled out)
reads of system, library and developer-tool folders
the temporary folder the interpreter compiles into
